summary.intent: Redesign the Ask Soony UI to win a hackathon (about 8 hours left): visualize routines, allow editing by text or drag and drop, and shape the demo story, using parallel UX/UI/jury expert agents.
summary.outcome: Launched five parallel expert agents (UX strategist, UI designer, jury devil's advocate, source researcher, data scout). The jury review came back first, and its safety finding was fixed and committed: routines may now only auto-execute free communication options, never re-plans, allocations or orders.

repo: Routines are in src/ask_soony/routines.py; whether an option is free is inferred from its cost text, which is fragile.
Evidence drawer (SAP vs Korean shipping advice with circled numbers on the scan) is the strongest feature and should lead the demo; routines work best as a closing twist.
Anchor logic lives in anchors.py and card tooling in cardtools.py; the project plan is in plan.md and the challenge brief in docs/challenge.md.
Routines run in a Monty sandbox with no network or files, are type-checked, dry-run on the live inbox, and handle each card once.

code.finding: `_costs_money` treated an option as free when its cost text was empty or 'none', so a re-plan/allocation could be executed automatically. Fixed by restricting routine actions to communication-type options, decided by type rather than cost text.

workflow: Run expert subagents in parallel with narrow, independent briefs and without revealing the preferred solution, to get unbiased critique.
Act immediately on safety findings from a review while other agents are still running.
Capture UI screenshots first so the design experts have shared material.
